chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a menstruating woman: should she wash the clothes that she wore during her menstruation? He said: “She washes whatever of blood has affected her clothes and leaves whatever is besides that.” I said to him: and she had perspired in them. He said: “Indeed, sweat is not from menstruation.”

(797) 84. And what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Asadī al-Nakhkhās, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a menstruating woman wears a garment and it remains on her until she becomes pure, then she should not perform salat (prayer) in it until she washes it. If she has two garments upon her, she performs salat (prayer) in the upper one of them. And if she has no garment other than one garment, then let her wash it when she menstruates, then wear it; then when she becomes pure, she performs salat (prayer) in it even if she has not washed it.”
So the manner of understanding it here also is what we mentioned regarding the first report, or it may be carried upon a kind of recommendation, which indicates that.

key_terms.الدَّمِ: the blood that must be washed if it reaches the clothing
key_terms.الْعَرَقَ: sweat, which is stated not to be from menstruation

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman have to wash all the clothes she wore during menstruation before praying in them?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on garments worn by a menstruating woman and clarifies that only blood must be washed from the clothing, while sweat does not make the garment impure. It also includes a second report about washing garments before performing salat (prayer), followed by a note that this may be understood in line with the earlier report or as a matter of recommendation.
